title: Import tariff on domestic firm investment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Method: Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed effects).  
Why: We have panel data with a clearly defined treatment group (steel/aluminum producers) and a sharp policy change that begins in period 4 (2018 Q2). DID compares the average change in log capital expenditures of treated firms before vs. after the tariff to the corresponding change for control firms.

Key identifying assumption – Parallel Trends: In the absence of the tariff, treated and control firms would have followed the same trend in investment. Additional assumptions: no interference between firms (SUTVA) and no simultaneous shocks differentially affecting only treated firms in the post period.

## 2. R Code
```r
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#  Steel Tariff DID Analysis
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Packages
if (!requireNamespace("fixest", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("fixest")
if (!requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("sandwich")
if (!requireNamespace("lmtest",  quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("lmtest")

library(fixest)    # fast high-dimensional fixed-effects
library(lmtest)    # for coeftest
library(sandwich)  # clustered vcov

# 2. Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s06_data.csv"
df   <- read.csv(path)

# Quick checks
print(head(df)); print(summary(df$y))

# 3. Vanilla two-way FE DID
did_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                 cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)

cat("\n=== Baseline DID result ===\n")
print(etable(did_mod, se = "cluster"))

# 4. Robustness check 1: Event-study (dynamic effects)
#    Relative time: 0 = first treated quarter (period 4)
df$rel_time <- df$period - 4          # tariff happens in period 4
event_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                   cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)

cat("\n=== Event-study coefficients (pre-trends robustness) ===\n")
print(etable(event_mod, keep = "rel_time::", se = "cluster"))

# 5. Robustness check 2: Placebo treatment one period earlier
df$placebo_post        <- ifelse(df$period >= 3, 1, 0)
df$placebo_treatxpost  <- df$treated * df$placebo_post

placebo_mod <- feols(y ~ placebo_treatxpost | unit_id + period,
                     cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)

cat("\n=== Placebo DID (fake start in period 3) ===\n")
print(etable(placebo_mod, se = "cluster"))

# 6. Summarise key numerical result
coef_est <- coef(did_mod)["treat_x_post"]
se_est   <- did_mod$se["treat_x_post"]
cat(sprintf("\nBaseline DID coefficient (log points): %.4f  (SE = %.4f)\n",
            coef_est, se_est))
cat(sprintf("Approximate percent change in cap-ex: %.2f%%\n",
            100*(exp(coef_est)-1)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
Economic intuition suggests the tariff raised domestic prices and profits for U.S. steel producers, freeing up cash flow for new investment. Hence we expect a positive treatment effect: treated firms’ log cap-ex should rise relative to controls. Magnitude: roughly +0.07–0.10 log points (≈7–10 % higher quarterly investment) in the post-tariff periods. Robustness checks should show (i) flat, statistically insignificant pre-trend coefficients and (ii) a null effect in the placebo DID.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=protected sector firms, control=unaffected manufacturers
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Tariff-protected firms increase capex relative to non-protected peers
_ground_truth.main_effect: 22% higher investment in treated firms post-tariff
